A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Distributed Event-Based Learning via ADMM and contain readable main text, equations, Figures 1–12, Tables 1–8, and Appendices A–G. Matching the text and visual material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original MNIST and CIFAR-10 training experiments, synthetic regression and LASSO experiments, packet-drop tests, and distributed graph experiments in Section 5 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their reported communication costs, accuracies, and convergence outcomes in Table 1 and Figures 3 and 8–12.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same ADMM updates, vanilla and randomized event triggering, and periodic resets. Restoring the agent index on d in Section 2 matches the existing definition and pseudocode. The new security-integration discussion introduces no implemented component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, CIFAR-10, synthetic linear regression, and LASSO, including the same heterogeneous-data, packet-drop, and decentralized graph scenarios in Section 5 and Appendix G.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, and FedADMM (Zhou and Li, 2023). Random agent selection remains the comparator in the graph experiments. Newly cited security methods are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: The protocols remain unchanged, including the 100/150-round MNIST/CIFAR-10 evaluations, client allocations, Dirichlet parameter, local optimization budgets, communication-load metric, and communication configurations in Table 2. Appendix G introduces no revised settings.

E4.justification: Appendix G retains the communication-threshold sweeps, communication-policy comparisons, and reset-period analysis with packet-drop probability 0.3 in Figure 10. The new security discussion adds no robustness test or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both Table 1 captions report averaging across different random seeds and standard deviations below 2%, without specifying exact run counts. Figure 11 retains minimum-to-maximum accuracy ranges across agents. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains all values, including 18,376 communication events for randomized Algorithm 1 and 27,000 for FedADMM at 78% CIFAR-10 accuracy. Figure 3 and Appendix G retain the same plotted outcomes. Figure 3's added annotation labels existing results.

T1.justification: The assumptions, convergence results, and derivations in Appendices A–F remain substantively unchanged. Appendix B changes gamma to gamma_k when choosing (k+1)^p; v2 already uses gamma_k in the preceding recurrence and the same subsequent substitution, making this a notation correction.

C1.justification: The abstract, five listed contributions, and main conclusion retain the claims about communication savings, heterogeneous data, accelerated convex convergence, nonconvex convergence, and packet-drop robustness. Added contextual and security-extension remarks do not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: The introduction adds a local-constraint/global-error interpretation and a connection to event-based estimation. Section 6 supplements the existing adversarial-attack limitation with a proposed robust-aggregation or anomaly-detection integration, claiming security benefits without sacrificing communication efficiency. This extension is not tested, and the privacy limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix G retains the same architecture descriptions, data-generation and preprocessing instructions, local solver details, and parameter Tables 2–8. Neither version adds or changes code-access, hardware, or other reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds Garofalakis and Samoladas (2017) for safe zones, Glasgow et al. (2022) for heterogeneous-data behavior of FedAvg, and Pillutla et al. (2022) and Yin et al. (2018) for security extensions. These provide limited additional positioning within the retained related-work discussion.

P1.justification: Edits comprise a few added explanatory sentences, citation insertions, and small notation corrections. The section hierarchy, contribution list, overall narrative, and Appendix A–G organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 and Algorithm 1 exchange columns on page 4. Figure 3 adds the annotation identifying Algorithm 1, its randomized variant, and FedADMM, with modest plot sizing and styling adjustments. Other changes are limited text and equation reflow; the figure and table sets are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves research context through the safe-zone connection and additional references, and improves clarity through consistent indices and Figure 3's added label. The security-integration suggestion remains untested and does not resolve the existing robustness limitation. The gains are limited to exposition and positioning; the theory and empirical support remain unchanged.
